name: Bacterial Transformation
description: Heat-shock transformation of chemically competent E. coli. Used for plasmid amplification or cloning. Adjust recovery time and plating based on vector and selection marker.
source_note: General educational template for heat-shock chemical transformation.

steps.title: Thaw competent cells on ice
steps.description: Remove a tube of chemically competent cells from −80°C. Thaw slowly on ice for 10–15 min. Do not thaw at room temperature or in hands — this reduces transformation efficiency.

reagents.name: Chemically competent E. coli (e.g., DH5α, TOP10, XL1-Blue)

steps.notes: Thaw until just barely liquid — still slushy is fine. Keep on ice until ready to add DNA.
steps.warnings: Do NOT refreeze unused competent cells. Efficiency drops dramatically after thawing.

steps.title: Add DNA to competent cells
steps.description: Add 1–5 µL of plasmid DNA (1–100 ng) or ligation reaction to the competent cells. Gently flick tube to mix — do not pipette up and down or vortex.
steps.notes: The ratio of insert:vector for ligation reactions affects efficiency. Use a positive control (known plasmid) to verify competent cells are working.

steps.title: Incubate on ice
steps.description: Incubate the DNA-cell mixture on ice for 20–30 min. This allows DNA to associate with the cell surface.

steps.title: Heat shock at 42°C
steps.description: Transfer tube to a 42°C water bath or heat block. Incubate for exactly 30–45 seconds (do not exceed 45 sec — cell death increases rapidly). The heat pulse causes DNA to enter the cells.
equipment: Water bath at 42°C or heat block at 42°C
steps.notes: Timing is critical. Use a timer. 30 s for most cells; some strains tolerate 45 s.
steps.warnings: Do NOT exceed 45 sec — longer heat shock decreases efficiency.

steps.title: Transfer immediately back to ice
steps.description: Immediately transfer tube back to ice. Incubate for 2–5 min. This cold shock step is important for transformation efficiency.

steps.title: Add SOC medium and incubate for recovery
steps.description: Add pre-warmed (37°C) SOC or LB medium without antibiotic. Incubate with shaking to allow expression of the antibiotic resistance gene before plating.
equipment: Shaking incubator or tube roller at 37°C
steps.notes: Recovery time can be reduced to 30 min for ampicillin resistance. Kanamycin and chloramphenicol require full 1 h recovery.

steps.title: Plate on selective agar plates
steps.description: Pipette transformation reaction onto pre-warmed LB agar plate containing appropriate antibiotic. Spread evenly using a sterile spreader or beads. For ligation reactions, plate entire volume; for plasmid re-transformation, plate 50–100 µL.

reagents.name: LB agar plates with antibiotic selection

steps.notes: Pre-warm plates at 37°C for 20–30 min before plating. Allow plates to dry briefly before inverting for incubation.
steps.warnings: Work near Bunsen burner or in laminar flow hood to avoid contamination.

steps.title: Incubate plates overnight at 37°C
steps.description: Invert plates and incubate overnight at 37°C. Colonies should be visible the next morning (12–16 hours).
steps.notes: Expected colony number: 50–200 for re-transformation; fewer for ligations. Compare with no-insert and no-DNA controls.

steps.title: Screen colonies and pick for culture
steps.description: Pick individual colonies and inoculate into LB + antibiotic for overnight culture (miniprep) or perform colony PCR to screen for correct inserts.
steps.notes: For blue-white screening (lacZ), pick white colonies for insert-containing plasmids.
